title: Sell Mineral Rights in Stonewood, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Stonewood, WV
metaDescription: Stonewood, Harrison County mineral owners: Clarksburg-adjacent legacy production, small residential lots, and severed mineral title checks.
heroLead: Stonewood sits adjacent to Clarksburg in Harrison County, where small residential lots often sit over mineral estates severed decades before current development.
intro: Part of the built-up area around Clarksburg, Stonewood's surface has largely been developed for residential and small commercial use, while the underlying mineral acreage in many cases was severed and traded separately long before the current buildings went up.

sections.heading: Severed minerals under a developed surface
paragraphs: As with much of the Clarksburg-adjacent area, current homeowners in Stonewood frequently don't hold the mineral rights beneath their property — those interests were often severed decades earlier and have followed a separate chain of ownership since.

sections.heading: Harrison County's legacy production backdrop
paragraphs: Harrison County's gas production history predates the Marcellus era substantially, and Stonewood-area tracts may carry older wellbores and leases still on record. Confirming current lease status and terms is a straightforward courthouse check, though the record itself can involve several older instruments layered together.

sections.heading: Why Stonewood's proximity to Clarksburg matters for title research
paragraphs: Because Stonewood sits so close to Clarksburg, some older deeds affecting the area were recorded using Clarksburg-area conventions or cross-referenced against city plats rather than standard rural township descriptions, which can add a step to matching an old deed to a current Stonewood parcel.

A title professional familiar with this area's specific recording history is the fastest way through that reconciliation, particularly for tracts near the Clarksburg boundary where older plats sometimes overlap.

faqs.question: Do I own minerals under my Stonewood house?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — check your deed for a mineral reservation, since many interests in this area were severed before current residential development existed.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family holds a severed mineral interest near Stonewood?
faqs.answer: A Harrison County Courthouse records search under your family name will confirm whether such an interest exists, independent of current property ownership.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Stonewood?
faqs.answer: Legacy production exists in the area; current activity depends on individual tract lease status, which is worth confirming directly.

faqs.question: Why would a Stonewood deed reference Clarksburg-area plats?
faqs.answer: Given the towns' proximity, some older deeds were recorded using Clarksburg conventions, which a title professional familiar with local recording history can reconcile with current parcels.

faqs.question: Should I expect my Stonewood interest to be small given the town's size?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — interest size depends on the underlying tract's acreage and unit participation, not the current population or footprint of the town itself.
